titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive supplies no title text, so both title-text fields remain empty. The raster restores the visible accents in FELICITACIÓN and CÓMO, joins the line-broken IM-/PRESAS as one word, and localizes the official twitch cues as *TIC*. It also renders the official heartfelt-card wording as tarjetas de felicitación and the final birthday card as regalo de cumpleaños. The official title text says the narrator privately likes Papyrus and expects typographers to object, confirming that the joke depends on the typeface's reputation.

regions.labelEs: DARLE A FRIKIS DE LA TIPOGRAFÍA TARJETAS DE FELICITACIÓN IMPRESAS CON EL TIPO "PAPYRUS" Y OBSERVAR CÓMO LUCHAN POR PARECER AGRADECIDOS.

applications.explanationEn: The le attached to dar points ahead to the plural frikis. Careful standard number agreement would normally use darles here; colloquial usage sometimes leaves le singular before an explicitly plural receiver.
Le attaches directly to the unchanged action dar and marks its receiver.

applications.exampleEs: DARLE A FRIKIS DE LA TIPOGRAFÍA
applications.explanationEn: Le inside darle marks the receiver, while a frikis de la tipografía names that same receiver explicitly. Because frikis is plural, careful standard Spanish normally uses les; the raster preserves colloquial le.
Tarjetas is plural, de links it to the kind of card, and felicitación remains singular as the classifier.
Impresas follows the noun tarjetas and its de felicitación modifier, then describes which cards are meant.
Impresas uses feminine plural -as to match the feminine plural noun tarjetas.
After luchan, por introduces the goal action parecer, so natural English uses “to” for this link.
Luchan changes for the plural people, por introduces their goal, and parecer stays in its unchanged -er dictionary form.
Parecer introduces an outward impression, and agradecidos supplies the description.
Agradecidos ends in -os because it describes the plural group of typography geeks.

cards.noteEn: Hobby is an English loanword used in Spanish. A common Spanish alternative is afición or pasatiempo.

cards.answerEn: to give him, her, it, or them; to give something to a recipient
cards.noteEn: Darle joins dar, the dictionary form meaning “to give,” to le, a small recipient word. Depending on context, le can point to a man, woman, thing, or singular collective. The recipient may also be named later with a, as in darle el libro a Marta.

example.es: Voy a darle la llave a Marta.
example.en: I am going to give Marta the key.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

cards.questionEn: Why can Spanish use le or les with a verb and then still name the receiver with a phrase beginning with a?
cards.answerEn: Use le or les with the verb, then use a phrase beginning with the word a to identify the receiver explicitly.
cards.noteEn: Le is for one receiver and les for more than one. It normally appears before a conjugated verb, but it can attach to an unchanged verb form, as in darle. The later a phrase clarifies who or what the short marker refers to; Spanish often keeps both pieces even though natural English states the receiver only once. In the prompt, the slash means that le and les are alternatives, each plus sign means “followed by,” and the dots mean that other words may appear between the verb and the named receiver.

Friki is an informal Spanish noun borrowed from English “freak.” The plural frikis can refer to enthusiasts with intense or specialized interests; tone determines whether it sounds affectionate or mocking.

example.es: Los frikis del cine conocen cada detalle.
example.en: The film geeks know every detail.

cards.questionEn: What common Spanish phrase means a card sent for a celebration or special occasion?
cards.answerEn: Use tarjeta de felicitación. Make tarjeta plural when referring to more than one card.
cards.noteEn: De links tarjeta to its purpose. In the plural, only the main noun changes: tarjetas de felicitación; felicitación normally stays singular because it classifies the kind of card.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.answerEn: often no separate English word; links a noun to another noun that names its type or use
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between two nouns where English uses a noun directly before another noun. For example, una taza de café is ‘a coffee cup,’ and material de oficina is ‘office material.’
Impresas is the completed-action form of imprimir used as a description. Its -as ending matches a feminine plural noun; masculine plural items would be impresos.
Con can introduce the tool, format, or style used to produce something. Natural English may use “in” or “using” rather than a literal “with.”

example.es: Imprimieron el aviso con un tipo sencillo.
example.en: They printed the notice in a simple typeface.

cards.noteEn: In printing and design, tipo can be a shortened way to refer to a tipo de letra, a typeface or font. This is distinct from informal tipo meaning “guy.”

example.es: Elige un tipo fácil de leer.

cards.answerEn: Papyrus is a widely available display typeface that many designers criticize as overused and visually clichéd.
cards.noteEn: Its faux-handwritten look appears in many informal signs and themed designs, which has made it a recurring target of typography jokes. Giving a carefully meant card set in Papyrus is therefore framed as an irritant to a typography enthusiast; the official title text adds that the narrator secretly likes the typeface and expects beautifully typeset complaints.
Luchan is the present form of luchar for they or plural you. Besides a physical fight, luchar can describe making a determined effort toward a goal.

example.en: They struggle to finish on time.

cards.promptEs: luchar por + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone struggles or strives to do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of luchar, then por, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Luchar changes for the person and time, while por stays fixed and the goal action keeps its dictionary form.

cards.answerEn: to; toward the goal of (after luchar)
cards.noteEn: After luchar, por can introduce the goal being pursued. When that goal is an action, natural English often uses “to” rather than translating por as “for.”

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something seems to have a quality or state?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of parecer followed by the describing word.
cards.noteEn: The description agrees with the person or thing: parece cansado, parece cansada, parecen cansados. This reports an impression rather than asserting the state as a fact.
Agradecidos describes more than one male person or a mixed group. A feminine plural group would be agradecidas.

example.en: We are grateful for your help.

cards.answerEn: for (introducing what someone is thanked for)

cards.noteEn: Bonito can come before a noun when the speaker presents a positive, often personal evaluation. Its ending changes to match the noun: bonita, bonitos, or bonitas.

cards.questionEn: What common Spanish phrase means a birthday gift or birthday present?
cards.answerEn: Use regalo de cumpleaños. Make regalo plural when referring to more than one gift.
cards.noteEn: De links the gift to the occasion. Cumpleaños keeps the same written form in regalo de cumpleaños and regalos de cumpleaños; only regalo marks whether there is one gift or several.

example.es: Le compré un regalo de cumpleaños.
example.en: I bought her a birthday present.
